title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
summary: In mid-451 CE, a coalition of Western Romans under Flavius Aetius and Visigoths under King Theodorid I checked the westward invasion of Gaul by Attila the Hun on the Catalaunian Plains. Theodorid died in the fighting, but Attila was forced to retreat east of the Rhine.

uncertainty.note: Fought in summer 451 CE; modern reconstructions often place the battle around 20 June 451.

as_recorded.value: BATTLE OF THE CATALAUNIAN PLAINS A.D. 451

where.historical_name: Campi Catalaunici, Gallia Lugdunensis / Belgica, Roman Empire

importance.justification: Checked the western military expansion of Attila's Hunnic Empire into Gaul, representing the last major military victory achieved by a Roman-led army in the West.

beats.caption: In 451, Roman and Visigothic forces confront Attila's Huns on the Catalaunian Plains in Champagne.
Attila's advance into Gaul is checked, forcing the Hunnic army to retreat eastward across the Rhine.

sources.title: Jordanes, The Origin and Deeds of the Goths (Getica)
sources.author: Jordanes; translated by Charles Christopher Mierow

sources.title: History of the Later Roman Empire, Vol. 1, Chapter IX: The Empire of Attila
sources.author: J. B. Bury

reviewer_note: Least sure of the exact location of the battlefield within Champagne, debated between Châlons-en-Champagne (Catalaunum) and the Mauriac plain near Troyes (Méry-sur-Seine).
